voiceover: Is there real evidence that Jesus rose from the dead? One of the strongest cases doesn't even start with the Gospels. The minimal-facts method, built by Gary Habermas and Michael Licona, begins with facts even critical scholars grant — and it begins early: a creed Paul received and passed on, traced to within a few years of the cross. Fact one: Jesus died by crucifixion — even the skeptic John Dominic Crossan calls it as sure as anything historical can ever be. Fact two: his disciples were convinced they saw him alive. And Paul, who once hunted the church, and James, Jesus' own skeptical brother, were both convinced they saw him too. What single explanation accounts for all of it at once? He rose. It is the best explanation of the facts — and it is what the first witnesses staked everything on.
